study.title: Why text a friend?
study.summary: A personal reminder can help a friend follow through on voting.

citation.title: Assessing the Effects of Friend-to-Friend Texting on Turnout in the 2018 US Midterm Elections

effect.label: Friend-to-friend texts in the 2018 study
effect.plain: About 8 percentage points among people whose receipt of a text changed because of the experiment’s assignment.

comparison.label: Large-scale organizational texts in other studies
comparison.basis: The published paper describes this as a meta-analysis average and cites Haenschen and Mann’s 2021 technical report, reference 15.
comparison.caveat: These numbers come from different studies. They are not a head-to-head test of friends and strangers.

caveats: The 8.3-point estimate applies to a selected group in one 2018 app experiment. It is not the average effect for everyone offered a text.
The 95 percent confidence interval was about 1.2 to 15.3 percentage points. Matching people to voter records and incomplete messaging complicated the analysis.
A follow-up experiment in the 2020 presidential election found a smaller estimate, with a confidence interval that included no effect.
This study does not establish that texting is always the most effective way to help after voting, or test an ask to text three people.

follow_up.title: Assessing the Effects of Friend-to-Friend Texting on Turnout in the 2020 U.S. Presidential Election

impactive_claim.assessment: Its 8.3-point result traces to the 2018 Outvote study. Cite the published paper instead of treating this vendor post as separate evidence.
impactive_claim.unit_correction: Use percentage points. The headline and some body text use a percent sign ambiguously.
impactive_claim.comparison_correction: The post and older working paper use 0.29 points for mass texts. The published 2021 paper uses 0.44 points.
do_not_reuse: a guaranteed increase for each text

study.display_note: Show the study caveats with the numbers. Do not present the two estimates as a head-to-head test or a guaranteed effect.
study.text: In a 2018 study of the Outvote app, people who got a text from a friend because of the experiment were about 8 percentage points more likely to vote. Mass texts from organizations averaged about half a point in other studies, so this is not a head-to-head test. A 2020 follow-up found a smaller effect that could have been zero.
study.cite: Schein and others, Proceedings of the Web Conference 2021

get_involved.title: Other ways to help
get_involved.intro: Start with a nonpartisan way to help. If you want to organize for a cause, the groups below describe their goals in their own words.

items.label: Become a poll worker
items.action: Use the official lookup to find your local election office. Check its requirements, training and sign-up dates.

items.label: Help someone get to the polls
items.action: Offer a ride or company. Check when and where to go with their election office.

items.label: Help a friend check their registration
items.action: Send your state’s official registration lookup. Let your friend enter their own details and check their status.

items.label: Swing Left
items.action: Join a volunteer orientation, call voters or knock on doors in competitive districts.

mission_quote.text: help Democrats win majorities at the state and federal level

items.label: Indivisible
items.action: Join a local group and use its action center to call or email your elected officials.

mission_quote.text: win an inclusive democracy and bold progressive policies

items.label: Turning Point Action
items.action: Join its local voter outreach events or use its app to help supporters follow through on voting.

mission_quote.text: embolden the conservative base through grassroots activism and provide voters with the necessary resources to elect true conservative leaders

items.label: Heritage Action
items.action: Join its Sentinel program for training, legislative updates and tools to contact your elected officials.

mission_quote.text: fight for conservative policies in Washington, D.C. and in state capitals across the country

poll-worker.note: The EAC lookup links directly to state or local election offices. This covers every state and DC without inventing state poll-worker fields.

get_involved.selection_note: Examples of ways to take part, not recommendations. Each side has one voter outreach group and one policy organizing group.

friends_family.label: Friends and family
friends_family.template:
Got a plan to vote? Here’s a guide to help you sort through your ballot: {guide_url}

If you’ve already voted, text three people and ask if they have a plan too. Message me if you have questions.

guide_url.source: the guide's public address (GUIDE_URL in src/views/pass.ts), whatever host the page is on
guide_url.note: Use the guide homepage, without saved picks, personal lookup details or a tracking query.

friends_family.audience: Private messages to friends and family

public.label: Work, school or public channels

state_name.transform: Resolve the state code through scripts/config.json stateNames. The generated state bundle already exposes name; Ballot exposes stateName.

registration_check_url.missing: Omit the entire registration line if absent. Do not claim registration is still open.

official_voting_url.missing: Do not offer the public copy button until this official state URL exists.

local_election_office_line.missing: Use an empty string and remove the blank line if the place or county is unresolved. Do not guess from a shared ZIP or choose the first county.

public.audience: Work, school, neighborhood and other public channels
render_rules: Build this message separately from the friends and family message. Never append the guide, a saved ballot or any partisan group link.
Substitute only the named fields above from the selected state and confirmed place. Do not reuse election_day.lookup_url as a statewide fallback.
Only use verified official state or local election links. Block copying if a required slot or template token remains unresolved.
Omit optional missing lines and trim extra blank lines. Preserve the closing offer to help.
Do not add a registration deadline, same-day registration, early voting dates or a polling-place promise from another state.
If two lines would carry the same URL (registration and official links in CO, GA and WA; official and local links in DC), keep only the first of them.

messages.copy_note: These are suggested messages, not quotations or claims that the sender has already voted. The ask to text three people is a practical prompt, not a tested finding of the study.
